implementation_notes: Since C++20 the filter collapses into a range adaptor: `view | std::views::filter(pred)` yields a lazy view over the elements that satisfy an `indirect_unary_predicate`, so non-matching messages are never materialised, copied or forwarded, and the criteria compose with `views::transform`/`views::take` into a Pipe-and-Filter chain. `std::ranges::copy_if` is the eager equivalent when the accepted set must be a container. A hand-written MessageFilter object is still justified when criteria are chosen at runtime from configuration, because a `views::filter` closure is a compile-time object.
pitfalls: The predicate is stored inside the view; capturing by reference a criterion object that dies before the view is traversed leaves a dangling reference.

For forward ranges filter_view caches the iterator to the first match, so a predicate whose answer changes between calls (mutable counter, time-dependent rule) breaks the view's invariants - keep it referentially transparent.
views::filter needs a viewable_range: returning a view of a local container from a function creates a dangling view, and a predicate that throws terminates the range loop.

variants.name: Polymorphic filter object (classic C++03 form)
variants.idiom_name: abstract MessageFilter with virtual bool accept(const Message&) plus a registry
variants.implementation_notes: The classic structure the pattern was written down with: one object per criterion behind a virtual `accept()`, selected - often from configuration - and applied on the branch between receive and send. With C++11 a `std::function<bool(const Message&)>` replaces the hierarchy when no per-criterion state or name is needed. Choose this form when filters are named components that operators configure, when several filters compose into a chain, or when the criterion must change without recompiling the pipeline.
pitfalls: A base filter without a virtual destructor corrupts state when the registry deletes through the interface; register std::unique_ptr or static storage instead of raw new.
One virtual call plus one object per message path: for hot in-process loops the closure form (std::function or a lambda) is measurably cheaper - measure before keeping the hierarchy.
Composing filters (a chain object) hides which criterion rejected a message; carry the filter name into the discard path or rejects become undiagnosable.
